Considering the submissions made by the learned senior counsel for the Petitioners and the learned counsel for the Respondent, CTUIL, the Commission ordered as under:_ _(b) The Respondent, CTUIL to file its replies/submissions within a week with a copy to the Petitioners, who may file their rejoinder, if any, within a week thereafter._ **_(c) In the meantime, having regard to the status of the Project, the revocation of the connectivity of the Petitioners shall be kept in abeyance and the Petitioners shall be permitted to carry out the various commissioning activities including First Time Charging and Trial Run Operation in respect of their Project till the next date of hearing._** _”_ - a) The Petitioner has filed successive Petitions seeking relief(s) arising out of the same cause of action, time and again. The Petitioner has repeatedly shifted the timelines for commissioning its project from one date to another after it had been allowed to convert its connectivity from LoA Route to Land Route in exercise of the power to relax. e) In the garb of a Petition seeking relaxation, the Petitioner is, in effect, seeking a review of the Order dated 25.11.2024 passed by this Commission in Petition No. 326/MP/2024. It is not open for the Petitioner to file successive Petitions seeking relief(s) arising out of the same cause of action, time and again. m) Further, this Commission, in its Order dated 25.11.2024, clarified that the ‘ _Petitioners’ Connectivity was protected from revocation by relaxing extant Regulation 24.6 on the ground that the Petitioners gave assurance that the project would be commissioned by 1.09.2024. Accordingly, the Petitioners ought to comply with the conditions stipulated in Order dated 21.4.2024 in Petition No. 283/MP/2024. Petitioners cannot seek further relaxations as per amended regulations since its Connectivity was allowed to be continued for meeting specific requirements_ .’ **11.** The Commission vide RoP of hearing dated 09.09.2025 reserved the matter for Order and further directed that the interim direction issued vide RoP of hearing dated 24.4.2025 will continue till the issuance of the order. **19.** We have considered the submission of the Petitioners and the Respondent. The following issues arise for our consideration: **20.** Petitioners have submitted that the Commission, by way of its Order dated 25.11.2024 in Petition No. 326/MP/2024, granted time to the Petitioners till 21.04.2025 for commissioning of its Project, subject to payment of compensation to CTUIL. Petitioners have submitted that they were committed to commissioning the Project by 21.04.2025, but the Project's implementation was significantly hindered by the continuation of agitation and continuous protests by environmentalists and local villagers against the alleged cutting of Khejri trees, which prevented the Petitioners from undertaking construction activities related to the Project. **24.** CTUIL has submitted that the Petitioners have repeatedly shifted the timelines to commission its project. It is not open for the Petitioner to file successive Petitions seeking relief(s) arising out of the same cause of action, time and again. The Petitioner has been holding on to the connectivity since May 2022, without developing the project, which is causing prejudice to other developers. _4. In response, the learned senior counsel for the Petitioners admitted that if the Commission so deems fit, the Petitioners are willing to furnish ‘reasonable compensation’ as a compensation for opportunity cost, to be credited to the common transmission pool. The Commission also queried the Petitioners and CTUIL on the aspect of the ‘reasonable compensation’, who in turn, sought liberty to file an appropriate affidavit in this regard.”_ **30.** Commission, vide RoP of hearing dated 24.04.2025, directed that the revocation of the connectivity of the Petitioners shall be kept in abeyance and the Petitioners shall As per the above, the Commission has rejected the Petitioner’s contention to provide relaxation based on the amended Regulations, as the Petitioners’ Connectivity was protected from revocation by relaxing extant Regulation 24.6 on the ground that the Petitioners gave assurance that the project would be commissioned by 1.09.2024 and Commission allowed 6 months’ time to commission the project ( i.e, by 21.10.2024).
